channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Burning wood for charcoal is destroying economic trees and threatening food security, officials say.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents lack succession path
item.description: The office has historically been used to balance political factions rather than cultivate future leaders.

item.title: Sierra Leone minister's actions defended amid calls for sacking
item.description: A "CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability" statement calling for the minister's dismissal is called 'policy vandalism'.

item.title: Namibia cuts spending to curb debt growth
item.description: Government revises expenditure down by 0.9% to N$105 billion amid a N$1.5 billion revenue shortfall.

item.title: Tanzania builds sports facilities for global events
item.description: The nation is investing in diverse venues beyond football to bid for major competitions like the All-Africa Games.

item.title: Zambia proposes K284.8 billion budget for 2027
item.description: Domestic revenue will fund 82.1% of the budget, a significant increase from previous years.

item.title: Namibia launches N$41.6 billion Dangote fuel project
item.description: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah commissioned the Walvis Bay tank farm and pipeline, marking a fast industrial breakthrough.

item.title: Tanzania hosts African ethics conference
item.description: Experts from Africa, Europe, and the US met in Dar es Salaam to discuss responsible business practices.

item.title: Four in five Senegal diabetes patients unaware
item.description: Nearly four in five diabetic people in Senegal do not know they have the disease, according to Assad.

item.title: FNB Eswatini offers repayment breaks to new clients
item.description: The bank introduced a campaign offering qualifying customers three-month repayment holidays on home loans and vehicle finance.

item.title: South Sudan NEC identifies 3,161 voter registration centres
item.description: The National Elections Commission will deploy 22,127 personnel for the exercise ahead of the December 2026 polls.

item.title: Tunisie Autoroutes plants 100,000 trees by 2027
item.description: The company will also maintain existing green spaces along its highway network as part of a broader environmental initiative.

item.title: Tanzanian law allows adopted children to inherit
item.description: The Law of the Child Act clarifies that adopted children have legal inheritance rights from adoptive parents.

item.title: ADF attack sparks Ebola spread fears in North Kivu
item.description: Suspected Ebola patients and high-risk contacts fled a health center after rebels attacked Cantine, raising alarms.

item.title: Algerian army to deploy in Niger
item.description: Niger's parliament approved the deployment of Algerian soldiers on August 30, 2026, following a request from General Abdourahmane Tiani.

item.title: Algeria launches initiative for 1,000 rural women entrepreneurs
item.description: The '1,000 Women: 1,000 Projects' initiative aims to transform traditional skills into sustainable businesses.

item.title: Ghana government allocates GH¢10m to media fund
item.description: President Mahama announced the 2027 budget allocation to boost journalists' welfare, training, and investigative work.

item.title: Three alleged robbers killed in Maputo shootout
item.description: Police say they encountered four individuals preparing to rob a microcredit business.

item.title: Togo opposition calls for national strike on November 20
item.description: The 'Warning Patriotic Day' aims to show public frustration with the Faure Gnassingbé regime.

item.title: Malawi HIV infections drop by three-quarters
item.description: New infections fell from 60,000 in 2010 to 14,000 in 2025, health officials announced.

item.title: Windhoek City disconnects water and electricity over N$932.7m debt
item.description: City CEO Moses Matyayi stated disconnections are a credit control measure, not punishment for residents.

item.title: Ivory Coast trains 31 new conflict resolution specialists
item.description: New mediators and arbitrators will help resolve disputes outside of traditional court proceedings.

item.title: Uganda hospitality sector urged to embrace green investment
item.description: Minister Nyamutoro launched a national initiative with Equity Bank to cut hotel operating costs and attract investment.

item.title: Libyan government proposes lifting fuel subsidies
item.description: Parliament member Ali Al-Tikbali stated the proposal came from the government, not the House of Representatives.

item.title: Kenya police seize 454kg of meth
item.description: Operation targeting international drug networks leads to three arrests and $27m worth of narcotics.

item.title: Ghanaian researcher targets digital security gaps
item.description: Johnnecia Agyemang's framework aims to improve cybersecurity policy compliance and management for US institutions.

item.title: Togo police block CNCC convoy, seize phones
item.description: CNCC leaders faced roadblocks and detentions on their way to a meeting near Tsévié on November 8.

item.title: Zambians urged to uphold integrity on Remembrance Day
item.description: President Hichilema led commemorations at the national cenotaph, laying wreaths for fallen soldiers.

item.title: Air Sierra Leone fails to restart London flights
item.description: The airline promised a late October return but has not resumed operations or provided verifiable evidence of flights.

item.title: Kenya sends condolences to Poland after Krakow shooting
item.description: Six people died and 16 were injured in a market square attack on Saturday, November 7.

item.title: Madagascar president urges faster national talks
item.description: Colonel Michaël Randrianirina acknowledged delays in the national consultation process, which began in 2025.

item.title: HRDC challenges NGO regulator in court
item.description: The Human Rights Defenders Coalition seeks to halt its deregistration by NGORA at a High Court hearing on November 12.

item.title: Praslin children compete in third 'Art Talent Quest'
item.description: Primary and secondary students from Praslin and La Digue created art inspired by local hotels.

item.title: Togo evicts informal traders before holidays
item.description: Journalist Dieudonné Sewonou criticizes the timing and lack of alternatives for displaced vendors.

item.title: Western Equatoria elects new athletics leaders
item.description: Four officials will promote athletics and build sports structures across the state’s 10 counties.

item.title: Cameroon gas assets part of US-Russia Ukraine talks
item.description: Lukoil's 30% stake in Cameroon's Etinde gas field is a bargaining chip in negotiations to end the Ukraine war.

item.title: Seychelles licensing official charged over permits
item.description: An employee of the Seychelles Licensing Authority faces charges for allegedly distributing driver's permits illegally.

item.title: Mauritius court denies bail for alleged cannabis trafficker
item.description: Marie Nathalia Laviolette remains in jail after the Supreme Court rejected her appeal for judicial review.

item.title: Nigerian manufacturers urged to deploy AI to cut costs
item.description: Industry leaders met in Lagos to discuss technology and financing for energy efficiency and competitiveness.

item.title: Muwua declares bid for DPP leadership
item.description: The 33-year-old PhD scholar aims to contest for the party's presidential nomination in 2030.

item.title: Liberia proposes record $1.538 billion budget
item.description: The proposed 2027 budget is the largest in the country's history, while extreme poverty also increased.

item.title: Nigeria's Flamingos win U-17 Women's World Cup
item.description: The team became the first African side to secure the FIFA U-17 Women's title after defeating Japan.

item.title: Liberia faces 323 more maternal deaths from funding cuts
item.description: US$2.4 million in reproductive health support lost since 2025, risking access to contraception for 327,700 women.

item.title: LAZ postpones hearing of complaint against minister
item.description: The Law Association of Zambia adjourned a hearing for a complaint against Foreign Affairs Minister Mulambo Haimbe.

item.title: DStv slashes subscription prices in Liberia
item.description: Satellite TV provider DStv reduces its Ultimate package from US$37 to US$7 monthly, making it more accessible.

item.title: G-100 chieftain says opposition consensus candidate plan dead
item.description: A chieftain of the G-100 group stated that the plan for a consensus opposition candidate has failed.

item.title: Malawi FA proposes K2.8 billion for youth football
item.description: The Football Association of Malawi's 2027 budget includes a significant allocation to boost grassroots development and talent identification.

item.title: Togo launches third male health campaign

item.title: CPC denies general Ndalé's death after defence ministry announcement
item.description: The rebel group claims seven fighters died in an attack, contradicting official reports of the general's demise.

item.title: Kenya to isolate preacher Paul Mackenzie in prison
item.description: Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen vows strict custody to prevent radicalisation of inmates following Shakahola massacre conviction.

item.title: Liberia launches clean cities initiative in 12 locations
item.description: President Boakai's administration aims to improve sanitation and create jobs for over 1,250 young people.

item.title: Cameroon court cancels 800 land titles
item.description: The Supreme Court's administrative chamber invalidated a 2005 land title and subsequent derivatives in Japoma-Bakoko.

item.title: Tinubu targets prosperity from economic stability

item.title: Mali ex-detainee recounts torture and deaths

item.title: Activist Demands clarity on detentions
item.description: Brebner Changala asks if Zambia is under a state of emergency due to continued detentions.

item.title: ASVP targets survival amid financial strain
item.description: Mauritian club ASVP focuses on budget prudence and squad renewal for the new Super League season.

item.title: 6 Setembro wins São Tomé championship
item.description: The team will now play Príncipe's 1º de Maio for the national title.

item.title: Bawumia urges parties to back long-term national plans
item.description: The NPP flagbearer proposed multi-decade masterplans for coastal erosion, flood control, and transport after Japan talks.

item.title: South Sudan named vice-chair for Africa at solar alliance
item.description: The nation will join regional discussions on solar energy development and cooperation among African member states.

item.title: Tunisia braces for higher temperatures and strong winds

item.title: Chapo launches 2026-27 agricultural campaign in Niassa
item.description: The initiative aims to boost production, food security, and agribusiness transformation.

item.title: Uganda minister promises more aid for Lacor Hospital
item.description: Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi will review financial support and tax exemptions for St. Mary’s Hospital Lacor.

item.title: Batangafo mayor appeals for hospital aid
item.description: The mayor of Batangafo Centre has asked the government to help save the prefectural hospital as MSF prepares to leave.

item.title: Mauritian sculptor Dhyaneswar Dausoa dies at 82
item.description: Dausoa, a pioneer of the fine arts department at the Mahatma Gandhi Institute, passed away after a long illness.

item.title: Mozambique proposes $250 million LNG solution for South Africa
item.description: Mozambique's state energy company seeks investment for floating units to supply South Africa's gas needs.

item.title: Ghanaian teenager killed in Toronto shooting
item.description: Toronto police are investigating the homicide of 18-year-old Prince Abdul Malik, identified by authorities as Malik Abass.

item.title: ACRA project mobilises Chad communities for child education
item.description: The ALAPAJ project is running a campaign in six Chad locations to promote schooling and protect girls.

item.title: Mage 4 stages theatrical rock concert
item.description: The band Mage 4 performed a unique show at the Mahamasina Sports Palace, blending rock music with theatrical staging.

item.title: Antananarivo city council warns dog owners
item.description: Owners must control dogs in public spaces and protect passersby.

item.title: Kinshasa deploys mixed brigade to ease traffic
item.description: A mixed brigade will regulate traffic on main roads starting Monday, November 9, to enforce circulation rules.

item.title: Chad's president names interim CEN-SAD executive secretary

item.title: Namibia cuts hake quota by 13%

item.title: Niger revokes nationality of over 20 people
item.description: General Abdourahamane Tiani's government has stripped nationality from critics of military rule.

item.title: Sudan conflict threatens CAR's Vakaga region
item.description: Refugee flows and arms trafficking fuel armed groups in the impoverished northern area, according to a new report.

item.title: Malian academics extend strike indefinitely
item.description: University teachers and researchers are entering their third week of industrial action over unpaid research bonuses.

item.title: Tundu Lissu convicted of incitement, sentenced to four years
item.description: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu was found not guilty of treason but convicted of incitement on November 6, 2026.

item.title: GNVB wins Coupe de Madagascar U23 doubles
item.description: The Gendarmerie Nationale Volleyball club secured both the men's and women's titles at the national U23 tournament in Antsirabe.

item.title: Ladies Makis win Madagascar's first Olympic medal
item.description: The Madagascar women's rugby sevens team secured bronze at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Rangers extend NPFL lead to 24 points

item.title: Boy dies after stepping on landmine in Macomia

item.title: MP urges Eswatini to tap E136bn local funds
item.description: Hhukwini MP Alec Lushaba proposed using local pension and insurance funds instead of foreign loans.

item.title: Eswatini food prices steady amid rising production costs

item.title: Céleste FC beats Aigles du Congo 2-0

item.title: Egypt train crash kills seven, injures 125
item.description: Two passenger trains collided in Al-Ayyat, Giza, on Sunday, leaving seven dead and 125 injured.

item.title: Association Nodde Nooto marks 30 years in Ouagadougou
item.description: The organisation honoured five partners for their contributions to development and humanitarian aid.

item.title: Mauritania's prime minister calls for national unity

item.title: Senegalese artist Boubou uses children's handprints for art

item.title: Spain seeks Morocco intelligence on Ceuta migration

item.title: Gaborone launches electric bus service

item.title: Sudanese army downs fourth drone in West Kordofan
item.description: The military reported capturing two towns and destroying RSF vehicles during intensified fighting.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea plans museums for archaeological finds
item.description: Government to establish sites in Malabo, Bata, and La Ciudad de la Paz to house artifacts dating from 50 BC to 1200 AD.

item.title: Tanzania aims for 70% domestic medicine production by 2030
item.description: Government has provided conflicting targets for local drug manufacturing, creating uncertainty about the goal.

item.title: First Lady attends West African bankers' awards
item.description: Dr. Fatima Maada Bio highlighted the banking sector's role in economic growth and development.

item.title: World Bank team inspects Abéché development sites
item.description: A delegation led by an urban development specialist visited bus station locations, a municipal slaughterhouse, and a school sports field.

item.title: Senegal pirogue capsizes off Lompoul, over 30 dead
item.description: A pirogue carrying migrants to the Canary Islands capsized on November 7, with 11 bodies recovered on November 8.

item.title: Satellite FC wins 2-0 to extend league lead
item.description: The Conakry club remains undefeated in Ligue 2 Pro after beating Tembou FC on Sunday.

item.title: Hajj conference and salon opens in Jeddah
item.description: More than 520 entities showcase services for transport, housing, food, and health.

item.title: South Sudan dialogue resumes to finalise resolutions
item.description: Political parties will meet in Juba on Monday, November 9, 2026, to discuss proposed resolutions from a two-week dialogue.

item.title: Libya ministry discusses water plant with Hungary's Rotary
item.description: The Ministry of Industry and Minerals met with Rotary International Ltd. to follow up on establishing a modern water desalination plant.

item.title: Morocco proposes tax amnesty for informal businesses
